_note: The layer effects/catalog.json was missing. That file says what an effect COSTS, in contended perceptual resources. This says why an effect WORKS on a person. A design decision needs both: an effect that claims no contested resource and exploits no principle is decoration.
_the_one_that_contradicts_naive_rules: Labor Illusion. People value things more when they see the work behind them, which is why a progress display that shows what is being done can beat a faster silent one. Any rule that says only make it faster is wrong about this case.
_upstream: Their four categories come from Buster Benson's Cognitive Biases Codex.

principles.name: Hick's Law
principles.says: More options leads to harder decisions

principles.says: People look for evidence that confirms what they think

principles.name: Priming

principles.name: Cognitive Load

principles.name: Anchoring Bias

principles.name: Fitts's Law

principles.name: Empathy Gap
